Block-device I/O for vinyl bstream reads, writes, copy, sync, rewind, and recovery.

# Purpose
This file implements the block-device I/O backend for `fd_vinyl_io`. It provides the `bd` storage engine that reads, writes, appends, copies, and syncs bstream data on a seekable device file descriptor. The code also manages the bstream sequence state, including `seq_ancient`, `seq_past`, `seq_present`, and `seq_future`, and it enforces block alignment, range checks, and device capacity limits before each operation.

The main public entry points are [`fd_vinyl_io_bd_align`](<#fd_vinyl_io_bd_align>), [`fd_vinyl_io_bd_footprint`](<#fd_vinyl_io_bd_footprint>), and [`fd_vinyl_io_bd_init`](<#fd_vinyl_io_bd_init>). [`fd_vinyl_io_bd_init`](<#fd_vinyl_io_bd_init>) sets up a new bstream or recovers an existing one by reading the sync block at the start of the device, validating its fields, and restoring the sequence state. The file also defines the `fd_vinyl_io_impl_t` method table used by the higher-level `fd_vinyl_io` interface, so this code acts as the concrete backend that connects the vinyl bstream API to a block device or file.
